claim: AI is a convergence machine; the signal layer requires knowing what is specifically yours and emitting it without distortion.
The most buildable thing and the most valuable thing are often different; the model can build what it is pointed at but cannot choose the worthy target for the operator.
Learnable taste is insufficient by itself; durable judgment comes from future-facing conviction or relationship and domain context the model cannot observe.
Knowing the signal is only half the job; it must travel from the creator's head into the head of the person it is for.
Source distortion occurs when founders compress familiar context past legibility and delete the customer pain that makes the technical work matter.

Organization distortion moves signal toward the average across management, legal, sales, and delegation handoffs; the proposed remedy is a thin function that carries original intent intact rather than more bureaucracy.
Machine distortion occurs when AI remixes a careful claim, evidence, and scope into derivative formats until a narrow result is heard as a broad promise.
Define the signal in one sentence with the limit built in and keep the promise and scope welded so the honest boundary cannot be edited out.
Before scaling, ask an unfamiliar recipient to describe the product back; the gap between what they heard and what was meant is impending distortion.
The ultimate outcome is trust, which is relational rather than fully gradable; humans define and protect the signal while AI handles convergent work around it.
